H&P – Super Detailed

Consult Summary:
25-year-old female with previously well-controlled asthma presents with 2–3 days of new wheeze, cough, and exertional shortness of breath unrelieved by salbutamol inhaler; advised to up-titrate preventer inhaler and arrange urgent face-to-face asthma review.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough.  
• Onset/duration: Began 2–3 days ago while running; persists, now occurs with brisk walking.  
• Progression: Persisting without improvement; salbutamol inhaler provides no relief.  
• Associated symptoms: No sputum production; denies infection symptoms.  
• Triggers/relievers: Physical exertion; blue (salbutamol) inhaler ineffective.  
• Previous control: Asthma well-controlled until current episode; last asthma attack 3–4 years ago.  
• Past exacerbations: Never hospitalised; no prior oral steroids or antibiotics.  
• Monitoring: Has peak-flow meter; baseline ≈ 380 L/min; no recent readings.  
• Review history: Last formal asthma review ~2 years ago.  
• Systems review: No other system complaints documented; denies medication allergies.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – long-standing; previously stable on inhalers; complications: current mild exacerbation.  
• Allergic rhinitis/hay fever.  
• Possible eczema (patient uses topical emollient and hydrocortisone; no formal diagnosis recorded).

Medications (patient-reported):
• Salbutamol inhaler (blue) – dose/route/frequency not documented (currently PRN, up to multiple times daily).  
• Clenil (beclomethasone) inhaler, brown – 3 puffs twice daily (patient to increase to 4 puffs twice daily).  
• Cetraben emollient – dose/route/frequency not documented (topical).  
• Hydrocortisone cream – dose/route/frequency not documented (topical).  

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• No smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use, or other social factors documented.  
• Lives at home (address confirmed); no information on occupation or exercise habits beyond running.

Family History:
• Brother – asthma.  
• Sister – eczema.  
• No other familial illnesses documented.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – teleconsult.)  
• Vitals not provided.  
• Chest examination deferred to upcoming face-to-face visit.

Investigations:
• None performed during consult.  
• Baseline peak flow (historical): ≈ 380 L/min (patient-reported).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Asthma – suspected mild exacerbation
  • Assessment: 2-3 day history of wheeze/SOB, salbutamol ineffective, no hospital triggers; possible need for step-up therapy.
  • Plan:
    – Increase Clenil (beclomethasone) to 4 puffs twice daily temporarily.  
    – Continue salbutamol inhaler PRN; may use every 2–4 hours if needed.  
    – Educate: If requiring salbutamol ≥ every 2 hours or if breathing worsens → attend A&E immediately.  
    – Arrange urgent face-to-face GP appointment within next few days for chest exam, peak-flow assessment, consideration of oral steroids and/or antibiotics.  
    – Provide asthma action plan reinforcement.

General plan items:
• No additional issues identified during consult.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: Current medication doses/frequencies, full allergy list, smoking/alcohol history, vitals, recent peak-flow, objective chest findings.  
● Internal conflicts: Medication name confusion – patient mentioned “Flanel/Bactroban,” clinician referenced “Clenil” as preventer (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor audio uncertainty around some medication names.
